output:
Short answer — choose an LED task lamp with high efficacy, good color rendering (CRI ≥ 80), a neutral/tunable color temperature (≈ 3500–4000 K for offices), dimming/controls and an ENERGY STAR or DLC listing. If you want a concrete product from your catalog I can pull specs; I found a “Harbor Task Lamp” and other “adjustable desk lamps” in your saved catalog, but those entries currently lack provenance/spec sheets in memory so I can’t verify their performance claims without fetching the manufacturer/spec pages.

Why that specification set?
- LED vs incandescent/CFL: modern LED task lamps typically use ~10–15 W to give the same useful light as a 60 W incandescent (≈ 800–1000 lm), so they cut energy use by roughly 70–85%. Example savings: switching a 60 W incandescent to a 10 W LED for 8 hours/day, 250 workdays/year saves ~100 kWh/year (≈ $15 at $0.15/kWh). (This is a typical calculation; verify the exact wattage/lumen numbers for any model.)
- Efficacy (lumens per watt): higher efficacy (≥ 80–100 lm/W) means better energy-to-light conversion.
- CRI (color rendering index): CRI ≥ 80 is adequate for offices; ≥90 if color-critical work is done.
- Color temperature: 3500–4000 K (neutral white) helps alertness and visual comfort in offices; tunable white (2700–6500 K) is best for HCL (human-centric lighting).
- Controls: dimming and occupancy/motion sensors reduce run-time and energy use.
- Certification: ENERGY STAR or DesignLights Consortium (DLC) listings are good evidence of verified efficiency and performance for commercial lighting.

Recommendations / product types to consider
- Best energy-efficiency (commercial): integrated LED task lamp with high efficacy (≥100 lm/W), occupancy sensor, and DLC or ENERGY STAR listing. Use these in shared offices or where you want maximum savings.
- Best adjustable/task control: adjustable-arm LED with a focused beam and dimming. Prioritize lamps with good shielding/anti-glare if placed near monitors.
- Best human-centric option: tunable white LED with at least dimming and multiple presets to support circadian comfort.

What I found in your catalog (memory)
- “Harbor Task Lamp” — present in your catalog entries.
- Generic groups: “adjustable desk lamps”, “task lamps”, “lighting products”, “desk accessories”.

Evidence status and claims requiring verification
- Evidence available in memory: only product names/categories (listed above). There is no provenance, spec sheet, or extractor data stored for those entries in memory, so I cannot confirm wattage, lumens, CRI, certifications, lifetime, dimming behavior, or price for the Harbor Task Lamp or the other saved items.
- Claims you should verify for any candidate lamp:
  - Rated wattage and lumen output (to compute efficacy and expected energy use).
  - Efficacy (lm/W) and lumen maintenance (L70 hours).
  - CRI and color temperature range (and whether tunable).
  - Dimming type and compatibility (triac, PWM, 0–10 V, Bluetooth, etc.).
  - Motion/occupancy sensor presence and settings.
  - Safety and efficiency listings: ENERGY STAR, DLC (for commercial), UL/CE.
  - Warranty period and driver replaceability/replaceable LED modules.
  - Photometric distribution (beam angle) and anti-glare features.
  - Price and total cost of ownership (initial cost + estimated energy savings).

Would you like me to:
- Pull full specifications (wattage, lumens, CRI, certifications, price) for the Harbor Task Lamp and any other catalog models? — I can fetch product pages and confirm claims.
- Search for specific ENERGY STAR or DLC-listed desk/task lamps in the market and compare models by efficacy, CRI, and features?
- Give a short prioritized shopping checklist for purchasing and deploying lamps across an office?

Tell me which you prefer (fetch catalog specs, search market-wide, or get a buying checklist) and any constraints (budget, style, mount type, color temperature preference).
